checks: Extremality forces every vertex to be in one of the generating fibers and to be a vertex there. Its fixed exposing functional has a positive gap on all other fibers and is strictly decreasing on every nonzero feasible tangent-cone ray. The bounded cone section has positive d-volume.

Nonincident facets have fixed slack and are inactive in a sufficiently small neighborhood. Thus each removed piece is the scaled tangent-cone slice, modulo the zero-volume boundary. The radius bound t_v=O(ε^(1/d)) is uniform in λ and makes the finitely many pieces disjoint even within one fiber.

The cuts intersect the same hull. Strict homothets toward interior points of each original fiber are retained uniformly for small ε and establish positivity and fiberwise Hausdorff convergence. The assigned mass sum is exactly ε, with zero weights yielding no cut.

An original cap strictly includes or excludes an entire sufficiently small piece when its margin at the vertex is nonzero. A coincident cap gives the displayed cone fraction at fixed base. The slab bound is width times projected area O(ε t_v^(d−1)), with vanishing interaction in dimension one under the avoiding condition.
Checked the exact source locators and matched all archived candidate hashes against the pinned graph.

overlap.comparison: The signed local mass result requires strict compatibility and unique own-fiber supporting normals, and evaluates fixed caps only away from changed marks. The frozen result permits polytopal corners, proves the tangent-cone scaling and covers cap coincidences.

readability: The ambient body may be considered in its affine hull if the bases have less than full ambient rank. The fiber-volume and compatibility assertions are unaffected.
review_method: Independent frozen proof review with exact arithmetic where applicable
summary: Simultaneous exposed-vertex cuts remove prescribed mixed masses exactly and preserve actual fibers. The moving-slab estimate uses the physical clipped tangent cone.
